title: If You Take a Mouse to School
author: Laura Numeroff

demand_candidate.rationale: Strong back-to-school buyer intent, predictable cause-and-effect structure, concrete school vocabulary, and excellent AAC sequencing potential.

hero.description: Small brown mouse wearing tiny blue overalls, the recurring star of the 'If You Give a Mouse' series, shown enthusiastically exploring the classroom
hero.source_note: This is the specific, recognizable 'If You Give a Mouse a Cookie' character in blue overalls — a generic Boardmaker mouse won't match; source dedicated clip art (e.g. TPT/Creative Fabrica 'If You Give a Mouse' sets) so students recognize the cover character.

book_summary: A boy brings his pet mouse (the same mouse from 'If You Give a Mouse a Cookie') to school for the day, and the mouse's escalating requests and antics — a lunch box, sandwich, notebook, pencils, and a spot in the backpack — lead him through a whirlwind of classroom activities including a science experiment, building a mouse house from blocks, and writing his own book. The story is circular, ending back where it began with the mouse asking for the lunch box again.

fringe_justifications.lunch box: The mouse's very first request when he arrives at school, and the story circles back to this same request at the end.
fringe_justifications.sandwich: Once given the lunch box, the mouse immediately wants a sandwich to put inside it.
fringe_justifications.notebook: After the sandwich, the mouse's next demand is a notebook to go with his school supplies.
fringe_justifications.pencils: The mouse needs pencils alongside the notebook, and later uses pencils and paper to write his own book.
fringe_justifications.backpack: The mouse wants to share the boy's backpack and is shown sitting inside it playing with a yo-yo.
fringe_justifications.blackboard: The mouse is pictured hanging off the top corner of the blackboard spelling out big words like 'adrenaline'.
fringe_justifications.experiment: The mouse conducts a science experiment in which purple matter erupts from his beaker, a signature classroom scene.
fringe_justifications.blocks: The mouse builds an elaborate 'little mouse house' out of blocks during his classroom adventures.
fringe_justifications.clay: After building the block house, the mouse fashions furniture for it out of clay.
fringe_justifications.book: The mouse collects paper and pencils to write and illustrate his own book, 'Goodnight Mouse' by Mouse, which he wants to take home.
fringe_justifications.yo-yo: While sitting inside the boy's open backpack, the mouse is shown playing with a yo-yo, a distinctive visual gag in the book.

grounding_note: Confirmed via multiple sources (Publishers Weekly review, School Library Journal review via Amazon/Beanstack, Barnes & Noble, HarperCollins listing) that this is the 2002 HarperCollins/Laura Geringer Books title by Laura Numeroff, illustrated by Felicia Bond, part of the 'If You Give...' series, in which the mouse from 'If You Give a Mouse a Cookie' spends a day at school. Scene details (lunch box, sandwich, notebook, pencils, backpack, blackboard spelling, science experiment, block-built mouse house, clay furniture, writing his own book, yo-yo in the backpack) are drawn directly from trade reviews describing the actual page content, so confidence is high.
